source_caption:
An American Carol is a political satire inspired by the classic story A Christmas Carol. The film follows a filmmaker who strongly criticizes American culture and patriotism. On a special journey, he is visited by historical figures and unexpected characters who try to change his views about the country and its values.

In An American Carol, the story uses exaggerated humor, parody, and political jokes to comment on modern society, media, and patriotism. The movie features appearances by several comedic actors and celebrities while mixing fantasy with satire. Known for its controversial humor and political themes, it became a unique entry in parody comedy films.

source_details.title: An American Carol
source_details.synopsis: An American Carol (released as Big Fat Important Movie in other territories) is a 2008 American satirical comedy film directed by David Zucker and written by Zucker, Myrna Sokoloff and Lewis Friedman. Using the framework of Charles Dickens' 1843 novella A Christmas Carol, the film follows liberal filmmaker Michael Malone (a parody of Michael Moore) as he is visited by three spirits to teach him the importance of Independence Day. The film satirizes liberalism in the United States, with focus on Moore's documentaries.
